decision.title: The sxml book: an mdBook whose examples are checked (packet book-1)
decision.summary: The user-facing book is an mdBook in docs/book/ in the style of The Rust Programming Language, and tools/check-book-examples.sh re-runs its examples, so a change that alters their output updates the book.

body.p: , after . The user-facing book is docs/book/, an mdBook (book.toml, src/SUMMARY.md) in the style of The Rust Programming Language: it teaches by running small examples, and has no internal process in it (no phases, packets or decision numbers).

item.p: Examples are real. Inputs live in docs/book/examples/<chapter>/ and the text shows them with {{#include}}. Commands and their output are ```console blocks. tools/check-book-examples.sh [BUILD-DIRECTORY] re-runs every block (each chapter file in a fresh copy of the directory its <!-- examples: NAME --> comment names) and compares the output, standard error included; --update writes the actual outputs back for review. The C chapter builds its programs with add_subdirectory of $SXML (set it to a snapshot of HEAD to check HEAD); the JavaScript chapter runs only with SXML_JAVASCRIPT set to a built package and is reported as skipped otherwise.

Who keeps it true: a change to the CLI's output, an error message or a result the book shows makes the check fail. The change that causes it runs the check (mise run book:check, about three minutes with the C chapter) and updates the book in the same commit.
Building: mise run book (mdbook build docs/book) writes build/book/, which is ignored; mise run book:serve serves it. mdbook is not a pinned mise tool; any 0.4 release works (0.4.40 here).
